prize_parts.citation: For the development of optical lattice clocks and their use in precision measurement.

statement.case_for: I now prefer optical lattice clocks. Katori and Ye made complementary foundational contributions to a precise measurement method whose scientific value is already demonstrated by reproducible clock comparisons and tests of fundamental physics. Its maturity does not depend on future applications or a redefinition of the second, and the two-person attribution gives the citation a clear scope.
statement.case_against: The clock field includes many contributors, so the historical record should establish which foundational advances belong to Katori and Ye and distinguish them from later refinements. The case is strongest when it rests on the physics and precision measurement already achieved, rather than projected applications.

responses.point: Kroll argues that optical lattice clocks are mature because reproducible precision and frequency comparisons already have scientific value, even as some future applications develop.
responses.response: I agree. The established precision and present use in measurement make this a strong case on its own; the prize need not rely on future applications. I would keep the citation focused on the development of the clocks and precision measurement, while asking historians to check the boundary between Katori and Ye's foundational work and later refinements.

responses.point: Eriksson argues that spherical-aberration correction made atomic-scale imaging broadly practical through complementary theory and realization, while noting that its development and attribution need historical scrutiny.
responses.response: That is a serious alternative: a durable instrument advance can merit recognition when it changes what experiments can resolve. I give the clocks priority because their foundational measurement advance and two-person attribution appear more bounded, though the history of later clock development also needs careful review.

uncertainties: The historical record should clarify the distinct foundational contributions of Katori and Ye and the boundary between their work and later clock development.
The relative priority of this measurement advance and other mature achievements, including spherical-aberration correction, remains a matter of scientific judgment.
statement.conflict_note: I direct WACQT and work in superconducting quantum circuits, creating a research and programme overlap with B037 and an adjacent overlap with B002. I have shifted my preference away from B037 in part because this overlap warrants careful review. The supplied profile identifies no direct personal connection to the proposed B037 laureates; the disclosed overlap should still be considered in any conflict or recusal assessment.
